Here you go — paste-ready wording for each term:

**Idempotency**

> An operation is **idempotent** if performing it one or more times has the same effect as performing it exactly once. Our API endpoints are idempotent, so clients can safely retry failed requests without duplicating side effects (e.g., a retried payment creation will not charge twice).

**Eventual consistency**

> The system follows an **eventually consistent** model: writes are acknowledged immediately, and replicas converge to the latest state over time. In the absence of new updates, all reads will eventually return the most recent value, but a short window of stale reads is possible right after a write.

**Backpressure**

> **Backpressure** is the mechanism by which a slow consumer signals upstream producers to slow down, preventing unbounded buffering and memory growth. When the consumer can't keep up with the incoming data rate, demand is propagated upstream and the producer throttles accordingly.

Two small style tips for the README:

- Use the noun forms (**idempotency**, **eventual consistency**, **backpressure**) in headings/glossaries, and the adjective forms (**idempotent**, **eventually consistent**) in sentences — that's the most natural pattern in English docs.
- "Backpressure" is one word (no hyphen) in most modern docs — e.g., Reactive Streams, Kafka, and Rx documentation all write it that way.

If your original Chinese sentences describe specific behavior (e.g., which component applies backpressure), paste them here and I can give you idiomatic full-sentence translations instead of generic definitions.
